- [RCTS.1.2.25] **`runtime_error`'s fields** — a fixture whose `expect.kind`
  is `runtime_error` pins a refusal. A harness must load the compiled
  artefact, edited as `tamper` says ([RCTS.1.2.21]), into a fresh engine, seed
  its cache as `cache_seeds` says, and give it the inputs in order until one
  is refused. The runtime passes only when the load, a seed or an input is
  refused, and the refusal satisfies every field below that the fixture
  carries.

  - `code` (required), a string: the status the refusal carries, as the
    negative integer in a string.
  - `message_contains`, a string or a non-empty array of strings: the
    refusal's text contains it, or each of them. A harness for a runtime
    that reports a refusal's reason as a value, not as text, must map each
    reason it can report onto one text, and must fail a fixture whose
    refusal has a reason it does not map.
  - `steps`, an array of objects, the session's inputs as [RCTS.1.2.28] has
    them, run on the harness's mock clocks; or `asserts`, an array of objects,
    each one assert, and `pump`, a boolean: those asserts in order, then one
    pump when `pump` is `true`. A fixture with none of the three has the load
    as its only input.
  - `cache_seeds`, an array of objects, each `{"key": K, "value": V}`,
    `{"key": K, "text": T}` or `{"key": K, "text_bytes": H}`, K and T
    strings, V any JSON value and H octets as two hex digits each, none of
    them `00`: after the load and before the first input, each is seeded
    under K, in order
    ([NLFC.9.1]). T is given to the runtime as the seed's JSON text exactly as
    written, which states a text no JSON value is read back as, such as an
    integer literal outside int64 ([LGRA.5.8.9]). H is given as the seed's
    JSON text, its octets unchanged, which need not be well-formed UTF-8: it
    states a text [LSTR.8.5] refuses, which no JSON string can. H holds no
    `00` octet: a U+0000 is [LSTR.1.5]'s refusal, which a binding makes
    before the call, so no harness could hand it over unchanged. V is given
    as JSON text with
    its members in the fixture's order, `, ` between items, `: ` after a key, and
    every character outside U+0020 to U+007E escaped: `\"`, `\\`, `\b`, `\f`,
    `\n`, `\r` and `\t` for those seven, and `\u` with four lower-case hex
    digits for the rest, as a surrogate pair above U+FFFF. So a limit on the
    text's length ([LGRA.5.8.6]) is met or broken alike in every harness.
    `runtime_fact_count` takes the field too.
  - `cache_cap`, an object whose members are among `keys` and `bytes`, each a
    non-negative integer: the engine's cache bounds, set before the load. A
    member that is absent or `0` sets no bound ([LSTO.4.7.5]).
  - `fault_at`, a non-negative integer: the input that must be refused,
    counted from 0, in `steps`, or in `asserts` with the pump after the last of
    them. Every input before it must be accepted. A refusal at the load or at a
    seed is at no input.
  - `no_fault_events`, a boolean: when `true`, the stream carries no
    `TypeError`, `BoundsError`, `ComputationError` or `EngineError` event once
    the refusal has happened ([NCBK.2.8]).
  - `fault_events`, an array of the names `type_error`, `bounds_error`,
    `computation_error` and `engine_error`: the stream's events of those four
    kinds, in stream order, are exactly the array.
  - `fact_count_after`, a non-negative integer: the facts live in working
    memory once the refusal has happened ([LERR.1.5]). Working memory is
    neither defined nor readable on a halted engine ([LERR.1.4.7],
    [NCBK.2.9]), so a harness must fail a fixture that carries it and whose
    refusal leaves the engine halted.
  - `halted_fault`, the name of a member of `EngineFault`
    (`proto/engine_fault.proto`): once the refusal has happened the engine has
    halted ([NCBK.2.9]), and its halt latch reports that fault ([NCBK.2.11]).
  - `last_event`, one of the names `fault_events` takes: the last event on the
    stream once the refusal has happened is of that kind. With `engine_error`
    it pins that the EngineError is the tier's last record ([LERR.1.4.7]).

  A harness must fail a fixture with no `code`, one whose value for any of
  these fields is not of the type stated here, one with `steps` and either of
  `asserts` and `pump`, one whose `halted_fault` names no member of
  `EngineFault`, and one that carries both `halted_fault` and
  `fact_count_after`. It must fail a fixture of any other `expect.kind` that
  carries `fault_at`, `no_fault_events`, `fault_events`, `cache_cap`,
  `halted_fault` or `last_event`.
